title: Beyond conventional MOFs: engineering next-generation electrochemical interfaces for ultrasensitive detection of analgesics and antibiotics
content: The increase in the levels of analgesic and antibiotic substances within pharmaceutical, biological, and environmental samples necessitates the development of methods that are rapid, specific and sensitive for analysis. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), with tunable metal nodes, organic linkers, pores, and interfacial functionalities, appear promising as interface materials for controlling enrichment and charge transfer at the interface. The present review critically analyzes the evolution from monometallic to bimetallic MOFs, conductive MOF hybrids, nano/2D MOF structures, molecular imprinting approaches, and MOF-based or portable electrochemical sensors for the analysis of analgesics and antibiotics. In contrast to prioritization of the sensors only on the basis of the lowest LOD values, we stress the important role played by the combined properties of the framework material, interface structure, electrochemical technique, selectivity, stability, reproducibility, and real sample analysis in defining the analytical potential of the sensors.
